 10/27/2026 Fond memories
 Key facts ahead of the Green-and-Whites' cup tie away to SC Freiburg. 
 Away to a team competing in Europe and currently among the Bundesliga's leading sides – it's fair to say the draw hasn't been particularly kind to the Wolves in the second round of the DFB-Pokal. Nevertheless, Tobias Strobl's side face an exciting challenge when they take on SC Freiburg on Wednesday evening (kick-off 18:00 CET) with a place in the next round at stake. The Green-and-Whites will also head to the Breisgau region with some encouraging statistics on their side. 
 The facts and figures
 Two of the 48 competitive meetings between the sides to date have taken place in the DFB-Pokal. VfL Wolfsburg won both. 
 The first of those two cup encounters took place almost exactly 20 years ago. On 24 October 2006, the Green-and-Whites secured a 1-0 victory, also in the second round, thanks to a goal from Mike Hanke. 
 The last time VfL faced Bundesliga opposition in the cup while playing in the second division, the national anthem was played before kick-off. It was the 1995 final, which the Wolves had sensationally reached before losing 3-0 to Mönchengladbach. 
 SC Freiburg also came close to reaching the final last season. The Breisgau side suffered a 2-1 defeat after extra time away to VfB Stuttgart in the semi-finals. 
 The two clubs sit next to each other in the DFB-Pokal's all-time standings. Freiburg are 20th with 231 points from 130 matches, currently eleven points ahead of the Wolves in 19th, who have played 126 games to date. 
 While the Lower Saxony side knocked out Altglienicke in the first round, Julian Schuster's team claimed a 5-1 victory away to Fortuna Düsseldorf. 
 Alessio Besio has a history with Freiburg. The VfL forward actually joined the Wolves from SCF in the summer, although he had most recently been playing up front for SC Verl. The Swiss striker scored six goals in 28 appearances for Freiburg's reserves during the 2024/2025 season.
